Authentication

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

Getting an API key

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits & errors.

Using the key

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}} {{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main\n\nimport (\n "context"\n "log"\n "os"\n\n "github.com/godzilladev/godzilla-go"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n client := godzilla.NewClient(\n godzilla.WithAPIKey(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY")),\n )\n\n pipelines, err := client.Pipelines.List(context.Background())\n if err != nil {\n log.Fatalf("failed to list pipelines: %v", err)\n }\n log.Printf("Found %d pipelines\n", len(pipelines))\n}}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}

Verifying webhook requests

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/1aaa9856-f563-4263-929f-16e234970286}}|prev_label=Quickstart|next_href={{cms:item/2df76640-838b-4256-956e-d8a19a602241}}|next_label=Building your first pipeline}}", "version_token": "43aa861c-8f67-4687-8ac1-dcec0a9fb8c8", "created_at": "2026-08-21T17:26:28.044Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-21T17:26:35.898Z", "placement_id": "a8665e39-d994-43d7-9f40-791673ac7d44", "folder_id": "24fcdf39-3a03-4f5c-90a5-886fdc1f234e", "file_name": "getting-started-authentication" } }
